question:
Whose administration became a model that was followed by Akbar when he consolidated the Mughal Empire?

[SSC CGL 2020]
options: Sher Shah Suri
Ghiyas ud din Balban
Iltutmish
Bahlul Lodi
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Sher Shah Suri

Explanation:
Sher Shah Suri (1540-1545 CE) established an efficient administrative system, which was later adopted by Akbar. He implemented key policies such as land revenue system (Ryotwari), postal system, road construction (Grand Trunk Road), and currency reforms. Akbar strengthened the Mughal Empire by following these reforms. Sher Shah's administrative efficiency is considered the 'foundation of Akbar's administration'.

Extra Facts:
☛ Sher Shah introduced the Rupee and Paisa currency system, which the Mughals continued.
☛ He built the Grand Trunk Road, stretching from Sonargaon (Bengal) to Peshawar (now Pakistan).
☛ After his death, the Suri Empire weakened, allowing the Mughals to regain power.

question_hi:
किसका प्रशासन एक मॉडल बन गया जिसका अनुसरण अकबर ने किया जब उसने मुगल साम्राज्य को मजबूत किया?

[SSC CGL 2020]
options_hi: शेर शाह सूरी
गयास उद दीन बलबन
इल्तुतमिश
बहलोल लोदी
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है शेर शाह सूरी

Explanation:
शेर शाह सूरी (1540-1545 ई.) ने एक कुशल प्रशासनिक व्यवस्था स्थापित की, जिसे बाद में अकबर ने अपनाया। उन्होंने जमींदारी व्यवस्था, भूमि राजस्व (रैयतवाड़ी), डाक व्यवस्था, सड़क निर्माण (ग्रैंड ट्रंक रोड), और मुद्रा सुधार जैसी महत्वपूर्ण नीतियाँ लागू कीं। अकबर ने इन्हीं सुधारों को अपनाकर मुगल साम्राज्य को मजबूत किया। शेर शाह की प्रशासनिक दक्षता को 'अकबर के प्रशासन की नींव' माना जाता है।

Extra Facts:

☛ उन्होंने ग्रैंड ट्रंक रोड (सड़क) का निर्माण किया, जो सोनारगाँव (बंगाल) से पेशावर (अब पाकिस्तान) तक फैली थी।
☛ उनकी मृत्यु के बाद सूरी साम्राज्य कमजोर हो गया, जिससे मुगलों को पुनः सत्ता मिली।

question:
When was the Battle of Tukaroi fought where Akbar defeated Sultanate of Bengal and Bihar?

[SSC MTS 2022]
options: 1564
1582
1575
1591
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1575

Explanation:
The Battle of Tukaroi was fought on 3 March 1575 between Akbar and Daud Khan Karrani, the Sultan of Bengal and Bihar. This battle was a significant part of the Mughal-Bengal conflict. Akbar's forces, led by his general Munim Khan, emerged victorious. Following this battle, the Treaty of Cuttack was signed, where Daud Khan ceded parts of Bengal and Bihar to the Mughals. However, Daud Khan later broke the treaty, leading to the Battle of Rajmahal in 1576, where he was decisively defeated.

Extra Facts:
Akbar launched multiple military campaigns to integrate Bengal into the Mughal Empire. Even after Tukaroi, rebellions continued in Bengal, prompting the appointment of Man Singh as governor. This battle strengthened Mughal dominance in eastern India.

question_hi:
तुकारोई का युद्ध, जिसमें अकबर ने बंगाल और बिहार की सल्तनत को हराया था, कब लड़ा गया था?

[SSC MTS 2022]
options_hi: 1564
1582
1575
1591
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है 1575

Explanation:
तुकारोई का युद्ध 3 मार्च, 1575 को अकबर और बंगाल-बिहार के सुल्तान दाऊद खान कररानी के बीच लड़ा गया था। यह युद्ध मुगल-बंगाल संघर्ष का एक महत्वपूर्ण हिस्सा था। अकबर ने अपने सेनापति मुनिम खान के नेतृत्व में इस युद्ध में विजय प्राप्त की। इसके बाद कटक की संधि हुई, जिसमें दाऊद खान ने बंगाल और बिहार के कुछ हिस्सों को मुगल साम्राज्य को सौंप दिया। हालाँकि, दाऊद खान ने बाद में संधि तोड़ दी, जिसके परिणामस्वरूप 1576 में राजमहल की लड़ाई हुई, जहाँ उसे पूरी तरह हरा दिया गया।

Extra Facts:
अकबर ने बंगाल को मुगल साम्राज्य में शामिल करने के लिए कई सैन्य अभियान चलाए। तुकारोई की लड़ाई के बाद भी बंगाल में विद्रोह जारी रहा, जिसे दबाने के लिए मान सिंह को गवर्नर नियुक्त किया गया। इस युद्ध ने मुगलों को पूर्वी भारत में अपनी स्थिति मजबूत करने में मदद की।

question:
In which city is the tomb of Emperor Akbar situated?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Chandigarh
Chennai
Varanasi
Agra
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Agra

Explanation:
The tomb of Emperor Akbar is located in Sikandra, near Agra. Akbar himself started the construction of this tomb during his lifetime, but it was completed by his son Jahangir between 1605-1613 CE. This tomb is an excellent example of Mughal architecture, showcasing a blend of Hindu, Islamic, Jain, and Christian architectural styles. It is made of red sandstone and features minarets at its four corners.

Extra Facts:
Akbar's Tomb is one of the most famous monuments of the Mughal Empire. The tomb is spread over a vast complex of 119 acres. Akbar died in 1605 CE and was buried in this tomb. The site is also included in UNESCO's tentative list of World Heritage Sites.

चेन्नई
वाराणसी
आगरा
solution_hi:

Explanation:
सम्राट अकबर का मकबरा आगरा के पास सिकंदरा में स्थित है। यह मकबरा अकबर ने स्वयं अपने जीवनकाल में बनवाना शुरू किया था, लेकिन इसका निर्माण उनके पुत्र जहाँगीर ने 1605-1613 ईस्वी के बीच पूरा करवाया। यह मकबरा मुगल वास्तुकला का एक उत्कृष्ट उदाहरण है, जिसमें हिंदू, इस्लामिक, जैन और ईसाई वास्तुशिल्प शैलियों का मिश्रण देखने को मिलता है। यह लाल बलुआ पत्थर से बना है और इसके चारों कोनों पर मीनारें बनी हुई हैं।

Extra Facts:
अकबर का मकबरा मुगल साम्राज्य के सबसे प्रसिद्ध स्मारकों में से एक है। यह मकबरा 119 एकड़ के विशाल परिसर में फैला हुआ है। अकबर की मृत्यु 1605 ईस्वी में हुई थी, और उन्हें इसी मकबरे में दफनाया गया था। यह स्थल यूनेस्को की विश्व धरोहर स्थलों की अस्थायी सूची में भी शामिल है।

question:
Udaipur was founded by__________after the fall of Chittor to Akbar in 1568.

[SSC MTS 2022]
options: Sawai Jai Singh
Raja Bharmal
Man singh
Rana Udai Singh
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Rana Udai Singh

Explanation:
In 1568, Akbar captured Chittorgarh, the capital of Mewar. After this, Rana Udai Singh, the ruler of Mewar, founded Udaipur in 1559, which later became the new capital. Udaipur is also known as the 'City of Lakes' and became a significant center of the Sisodia dynasty. Rana Udai Singh shifted from Chittor to Udaipur to escape Akbar's invasions and established it as a safer stronghold.

Extra Facts:
Mewar was a prominent Rajput kingdom in Rajasthan that resisted Mughal dominance for a long time. Maharana Pratap, son of Rana Udai Singh, fought against Akbar's forces in the Battle of Haldighati (1576). Udaipur's City Palace and Jag Mandir are historically significant landmarks.

question:
What is the real name of Babur?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Salim
Khurrum
Nashruddin
Zahir-ud-din
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Zahir-ud-din

Explanation:
Babur's real name was Zahir-ud-din Muhammad Babur. He was the founder of the Mughal Empire and established Mughal rule in India after defeating Ibrahim Lodi in the First Battle of Panipat (1526). Babur was a descendant of Timur and Genghis Khan. He wrote his autobiography, 'Baburnama', in Chagatai Turkic, which is a crucial source of Mughal history.

Extra Facts:
Babur was born in 1483 in Fergana (present-day Uzbekistan). He became the ruler of Fergana at the age of 12 but soon lost his kingdom. He strengthened his power by capturing Kabul and later invaded India. His army effectively used tulughma tactics and artillery, which helped him win the Battle of Panipat.

question_hi:
बाबर का वास्तविक नाम क्या है?

[RRB NTPC CBT]

खुर्रुम
नशरुद्दीन
ज़हीर-उद-दीन
solution_hi:

Explanation:
बाबर का वास्तविक नाम ज़हीर-उद-दीन मुहम्मद बाबर था। वह मुग़ल साम्राज्य का संस्थापक था और उसने 1526 में पानीपत की पहली लड़ाई में इब्राहिम लोदी को हराकर भारत में मुग़ल शासन की नींव रखी। बाबर तैमूर और चंगेज खान का वंशज था। उसने अपनी आत्मकथा 'बाबरनामा' लिखी, जो चगताई तुर्क भाषा में है और मुग़ल इतिहास का एक महत्वपूर्ण स्रोत है।

Extra Facts:
बाबर का जन्म 1483 में फरगना (वर्तमान उज़्बेकिस्तान) में हुआ था। वह 12 साल की उम्र में ही फरगना का शासक बना, लेकिन जल्द ही उसे अपना राज्य छोड़ना पड़ा। उसने काबुल पर कब्ज़ा करके अपनी शक्ति को मजबूत किया और बाद में भारत पर आक्रमण किया। उसकी सेना ने तुलुगमा युद्धनीति और तोपखाने का प्रभावी उपयोग किया, जिससे वह पानीपत की लड़ाई में विजयी हुआ।

question:
Takht - e - Akbari Platform on which Akbar was crowned as emperor lies in state of ________

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Rajasthan
Punjab
Haryana
Uttar Pradesh
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Punjab

Explanation:
The Takht-e-Akbari is the throne where Akbar was crowned as the Mughal emperor on 14th February 1556. This platform is located in Kalanaur, Punjab. After the death of his father Humayun, Akbar was declared emperor here, as he was only 13 years old and too young to ascend the throne in Delhi. This event marked a significant turning point in Mughal history, as Akbar later established a vast empire.

Extra Facts:
Kalanaur is a small village presently located in the Hoshiarpur district of Punjab. Akbar's coronation took place under the guardianship of Bairam Khan, who assisted him in the early years of his reign. This site holds historical importance as it symbolizes the beginning of the golden era of the Mughal Empire.

question:
The Mughal court chronicles are written in _____

[SSC CGL 2021]
options: Arabic
Persian
Turkish
Urdu
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Persian

Explanation:
The Mughal court chronicles were primarily written in Persian. During the Mughal Empire, Persian was the official and cultural language preferred by the rulers, scholars, and courtiers. It was extensively used in administration, literature, and historical documentation. Under Akbar's reign, Persian was further promoted, and notable works like 'Akbarnama' (by Abul Fazl) and 'Baburnama' (Babur's autobiography) were composed in this language. Persian was not only the medium for administrative work but also for literary and historical writings.

Extra Facts:
Apart from Persian, Chagatai Turkish was also used during the Mughal period as it was the native language of the Mughal rulers. However, Persian gradually replaced it. Even during the reigns of Shah Jahan and Aurangzeb, Persian remained the dominant language. The Mughal court patronized Persian poets and writers, which contributed to the flourishing of this language.

solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है फारसी

Explanation:
मुगल दरबार के इतिहास मुख्य रूप से फारसी भाषा में लिखे गए हैं। मुगल साम्राज्य के दौरान, फारसी को राजकीय और सांस्कृतिक भाषा के रूप में प्राथमिकता दी जाती थी। यह भाषा मुगल शासकों, विद्वानों और दरबारियों द्वारा व्यापक रूप से प्रयोग की जाती थी। अकबर के शासनकाल में फारसी को और अधिक बढ़ावा मिला, और इसी भाषा में प्रसिद्ध ग्रंथ जैसे 'अकबरनामा' (अबुल फजल द्वारा लिखित) और 'बाबरनामा' (बाबर की आत्मकथा) लिखे गए। फारसी न केवल प्रशासनिक कार्यों में बल्कि साहित्य और इतिहास लेखन में भी प्रमुख थी।

Extra Facts:
मुगल काल में फारसी के अलावा चगताई तुर्की भी प्रयोग में थी, क्योंकि मुगल शासकों की मूल भाषा यही थी। हालांकि, धीरे-धीरे फारसी ने इसका स्थान ले लिया। शाहजहाँ और औरंगजेब के समय में भी फारसी ही प्रमुख भाषा रही। मुगल दरबार में फारसी कवियों और लेखकों को विशेष सम्मान दिया जाता था, जिससे इस भाषा का विकास हुआ।

Who among the following rulers built five astronomical observatories at different places in north India?

solution:

Explanation:

He built five astronomical observatories (Jantar Mantar) in North India, located in Delhi, Jaipur, Ujjain, Mathura, and Varanasi. These observatories were designed for astronomical calculations and observations. Jai Singh collaborated with European and Indian astronomers for their construction. He also authored texts like Jai Singh Kārikā and Samrāt Siddhānta.

Extra Facts:
Jai Singh II founded the city of Jaipur in 1727 CE, planned according to Vastu Shastra. He attempted to bridge European and Indian sciences and commissioned the Persian translation of the astronomical text Zīj-i Muhammad Shāhī.

question:
The Buland Darwaja at Fatehpur Sikri was erected by Akbar to celebrate his conquest of _______.

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Bengal
Mewar
Kashmir
Gujarat
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Gujarat

Explanation:
The Buland Darwaza was built by Emperor Akbar in 1575 CE to commemorate his victory over Gujarat. It is located in Fatehpur Sikri, which served as Akbar's capital. This victory occurred in 1572-73 CE when Akbar defeated the rebellious chieftains of Gujarat and annexed the region into the Mughal Empire. The Buland Darwaza stands 54 meters tall and is also known as the 'Gate of Magnificence'. It is constructed using red sandstone and marble.

Extra Facts:
Fatehpur Sikri was established as Akbar's capital in 1571 CE but was abandoned in 1585 CE due to water scarcity. The site houses significant monuments like the Diwan-i-Khas, Panch Mahal, Jodha Bai's Palace, and the Tomb of Sheikh Salim Chishti. Akbar promoted Sulh-e-Kul (peace with all religions) and invited scholars of various faiths here.

question:
Who amongst the following Mughal emperors got classical Hindu mythological texts Ramayana and Mahabharata translated into Persian ?

This translation was carried out by his court scholars, such as Abdul Qadir Badayuni and Faizi. The translated works are known as 'Razmnama' (Persian version of Mahabharata) and 'Ramayana'. This initiative reflects Akbar's tolerance and interest in Indian culture.

Extra Facts:
Akbar established the Ibadat Khana in Fatehpur Sikri, where scholars of different religions held discussions. He also introduced a new syncretic religion called Din-e-Ilahi. Akbar's reign is considered the Golden Age of the Mughal Empire, marked by advancements in art, literature, and architecture.

question:
According to Mughal records, during Akbar's reign, there were 29 Mansabdars with a rank of_______.

[CONSTABLE EXE 2023]
options: 2,500 zat
5,000 zat
7,000 zat
500 zat
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 5,000 zat

Explanation:
The Mansabdari system was a military and administrative framework introduced by Akbar in the Mughal Empire. It classified officials based on their 'zat' (personal rank) and 'sawar' (number of cavalrymen). During Akbar's reign, 29 Mansabdars held the prestigious rank of 5,000 zat. This high-ranking position was reserved for influential military and administrative officers who played key roles in governance. Akbar strengthened centralized rule through this system and systematically enhanced the empire's military capabilities.

Extra Facts:
Akbar's Mansabdari system had 33 grades, ranging from the lowest (10 zat) to the highest (10,000 zat, e.g., Raja Man Singh). Mansabdars received salaries either in cash or as jagirs (land grants). This system provided the Mughal Empire with an organized military-administrative structure, facilitating expansion and stability.

Explanation:

Extra Facts:
मनसबदारी प्रणाली में अकबर ने 33 ग्रेड बनाए थे, जिनमें सबसे निचली रैंक 10 जात और सबसे ऊँची 10,000 जात (जैसे राजा मान सिंह) थी। मनसबदारों को नकद वेतन या जागीर (भूमि अनुदान) दिया जाता था। इस प्रणाली ने मुगल साम्राज्य को एक सुसंगठित सैन्य-प्रशासनिक ढाँचा प्रदान किया, जिससे साम्राज्य का विस्तार और स्थायित्व संभव हुआ।

question:
Which Mughal ruler was responsible for the execution of Guru Tegh Bahadur in the year 1675?

Guru Tegh Bahadur was executed in 1675 on the orders of the Mughal ruler Aurangzeb. This event occurred due to his refusal to convert to Islam and his stand to protect Hindu religious rights. Guru Tegh Bahadur opposed Aurangzeb's forced conversions and defended the Kashmiri Pandits' religious freedom. As a result, he was tortured in Delhi and later beheaded. This event marked a turning point in Sikh history, leading Guru Gobind Singh to establish the Khalsa Panth.

Extra Facts:
Aurangzeb implemented strict Islamic policies during his reign (1658-1707), including the destruction of Hindu temples, imposition of Jizya tax, and persecution of non-Muslims. His harsh treatment of Sikh Gurus fueled rebellion among Sikhs. Guru Tegh Bahadur's martyrdom inspired Sikhs to unite and fight for religious freedom.

question:
Who among the following Mughal Emperors had assumed the title of Padshah?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Jahangir
Babur
Humayun
Akbar
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Babur

Explanation:
Babur was the first Mughal emperor to assume the title of 'Padshah', a Persian term meaning 'Emperor' or 'Great Ruler'. After defeating Ibrahim Lodi in the First Battle of Panipat (1526), he established the Mughal Empire in India and declared himself 'Padshah-e-Hind'. This title symbolized supreme sovereignty and was later used by Akbar, Jahangir, Shah Jahan, and Aurangzeb.

Extra Facts:
Babur wrote his autobiography, 'Baburnama' (Tuzuk-e-Babri), detailing his life and conquests. He was a descendant of Timur and Genghis Khan. His use of gunpowder artillery and Ottoman tactics helped him defeat Ibrahim Lodi. Babur laid the foundation of the Mughal Empire, which lasted for nearly 300 years.

question:
The famous monument, Aram Bagh, was built by Babur. It is located in__________.

[SSC CHSL 2022]
options: Delhi
Uttar Pradesh
Madhya Pradesh
Bihar
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Uttar Pradesh

Explanation:
Aram Bagh is the oldest Mughal garden in India, built by the first Mughal emperor Babur in 1528 CE. It is located in Agra, Uttar Pradesh. Babur designed it in the Persian-style and originally named it 'Bagh-e-Nur Afshan' (Nur Afshan Garden). This garden is an excellent example of Mughal architecture and follows the Charbagh (divided into four parts) layout. Later, Jahangir renamed it 'Aram Bagh' (Garden of Rest) as he used to relax here.

Extra Facts:
Babur built several gardens in India, with Aram Bagh being the most famous. He mentioned these gardens in his autobiography 'Baburnama'. The Mughals popularized the Persian garden style in India, featuring water channels, fountains, and symmetrical designs. Apart from Aram Bagh, Shalimar Bagh (Lahore) and Humayun’s Tomb Garden (Delhi) are other famous Mughal gardens.

बाबर ने भारत में कई उद्यान बनवाए, जिनमें आराम बाग सबसे प्रसिद्ध है। उसने अपनी आत्मकथा 'बाबरनामा' में भी इन उद्यानों का उल्लेख किया है। मुगलों ने भारत में फारसी उद्यान शैली को लोकप्रिय बनाया, जिसमें पानी की नहरें, फव्वारे और सममित डिजाइन प्रमुख थे। आराम बाग के अलावा, शालीमार बाग (लाहौर) और हुमायूँ का मकबरा उद्यान (दिल्ली) भी मुगल उद्यानों के प्रसिद्ध उदाहरण हैं।

question:
Who among the following issued Mahzarnama in 1579?

[SSC CGL 2020]
options: Humayun
Jahangir
Shah Jahan
Akbar
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Akbar

Explanation:
The Mahzarnama was a religious decree issued by the Mughal Emperor Akbar in 1579. Its primary purpose was to establish Akbar as the supreme authority in religious matters. Through this decree, Akbar declared himself as 'Imam-e-Adil' (Just Ruler) and positioned his authority above the fatwas of the ulema. This move was part of Akbar's policy of 'Din-e-Ilahi' (a universal religion), where he aimed to unify various religions under one umbrella. The Mahzarnama reflected Akbar's religious tolerance and imperial policies.

Extra Facts:
The Mahzarnama had a profound impact on the Mughal Empire. It solidified Akbar's position as the supreme leader in both religious and political spheres. The document was signed by prominent ulema and religious leaders, further strengthening Akbar's authority. It also symbolized Akbar's policy of 'Sulh-e-Kul' (peace with all), promoting Hindu-Muslim unity.

question:
By which name is the historical road built by Sher Shah Suri known?

[SSC CGL 2022]
options: Grand trunk road
Express way
Highway
Cart road
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Grand trunk road

Explanation:
Sher Shah Suri constructed a vast road network during his reign (1540-1545 CE), among which the 'Sadak-e-Azam' (later named Grand Trunk Road) was the most significant. It stretched from Sonargaon (Bengal) to Peshawar (now Pakistan). The purpose was to facilitate military movement, trade, and communication. Sher Shah incorporated caravanserais (rest houses), planted trees, and distance markers, reflecting his administrative vision. The British later expanded it and renamed it GT Road.

Extra Facts:
Sher Shah Suri defeated Mughal emperor Humayun and established the Sur Empire. His other reforms include introduction of the Rupee coin, land revenue system (Rai), and postal system. He died in 1545 CE during the siege of Kalinjar Fort.
